title: Accessibility of simplicial-space local equivalences
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$ of small sets and $\mathrm{sS}=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}},\mathrm{sSet})$ with the Reedy model structure and mapping simplicial sets of [lem-coef-simplicial-space-reedy-cartesian]. A monomorphism is a map injective in every bidegree. Fix a monomorphism $f:P\hookrightarrow Q$. Call $Z$ $f$-local if it is Reedy fibrant and $\operatorname{Map}(Q,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}(P,Z)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, with weak homotopy equivalences as in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Let $W_f^{\mathrm{mono}}$ be the full subcategory of $\mathrm{sS}^{[1]}$ on monomorphisms $u:X\hookrightarrow Y$ for which $\operatorname{Map}(Y,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}(X,Z)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every $f$-local $Z$. Objects of the arrow category are arrows and its morphisms are commuting squares; its colimits are computed at source and target. Then $W_f^{\mathrm{mono}}$ is replete and accessible as a subcategory: for some infinite regular small cardinal $\lambda$ it is closed under small $\lambda$-filtered colimits computed in the arrow category and is generated under those colimits by a small family of its objects. Replete means closed under isomorphisms in the arrow category. Here $\lambda$-filtered means that every diagram with fewer than $\lambda$ morphisms admits a cocone, and regular means unions of fewer than $\lambda$ sets of size less than $\lambda$ have size less than $\lambda$. The cardinal $\lambda$ depends only on $f$ and the fixed universe. No localized model structure is assumed.

source.place: Barwick, On left and right model categories and left and right Bousfield localizations, Lemmas 4.5–4.6, printed p. 43, for all local equivalences; the additional intersection with degreewise monomorphisms is an agent-formulated accessibility specialization, not a verbatim claim of Lemma 4.6. Read online 2026-10-17, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this homotopical accessibility result.

proof.text: Put $D=\Delta\times\Delta$ and $\mathcal M=\mathrm{sS}=\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},\mathrm{Set}_{\mathcal U})$. By [lem-coef-presheaf-local-presentability], $\mathcal M$ is locally presentable. The same holds for $\mathcal M^{[1]}$, $\mathcal M\times\mathcal M$, and $(\mathcal M\times\mathcal M)^{[1]}$: they are set-valued presheaf categories on the small categories $D\times[1]^{\mathrm{op}}$, $D\amalg D$, and $(D\amalg D)\times[1]^{\mathrm{op}}$, respectively. The identification is just currying; its maps and colimits are componentwise. All generators and indexing sets below are small in this same universe.

source.place: Appendix A.2.6, presentable ambient categories; presheaf instances as cited.

proof.text: Write $a_n:\partial F(n)\hookrightarrow F(n)$, where $\partial F(n)$ is the union of the images of proper injective faces in the outer representable, discrete in the inner direction; $\partial F(0)=\varnothing$. Let $b_m:\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$ and $h_{m,k}:\Lambda_k^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$. Define small sets $I_R=\{a_n\square cb_m\}$ and $J_R=\{a_n\square ch_{m,k}\}$, where $\square$ is the cartesian pushout product of [lem-coef-simplicial-space-reedy-cartesian]. For any $p:U\to V$, a square against $a_n\square ct$ is exactly a square against $t$ for the matching map $U_n\to V_n\times_{M_nV}M_nU$: a map out of $F(n)$ specifies its degree-$n$ value, and restriction to $\partial F(n)$ specifies the compatible values on all proper outer faces. This is [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection] and the limit description of $M_n$ in [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Thus the horn and boundary lifting characterizations in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] give $J_R^{\square}=\mathrm{Fib}_R$ and $I_R^{\square}=\mathrm{Fib}_R\cap W_R$, including the degree-zero cases.

source.place: Notation 3.32 and Lemma 3.33, printed p. 34; the matching-map lifting identification is expanded here.

proof.text: Every object of $\mathcal M$ is Reedy cofibrant, since its initial map is bidegreewise injective, and the cofibrations are the monomorphisms by [lem-coef-simplicial-space-reedy-cartesian]. Every $a_n$ and every $ct$ above is a Reedy cofibration. When $t$ is a horn inclusion, $ct$ is also a Reedy weak equivalence: its value at every outer degree is that trivial Kan cofibration, by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] and the objectwise weak equivalences of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. The pushout-product assertion of [lem-coef-simplicial-space-reedy-cartesian] consequently makes every member of $J_R$ a Reedy trivial cofibration. In particular, for every Reedy fibrant $Z$, $\operatorname{Map}(j,Z)$ is a trivial Kan fibration for $j\in J_R$.

source.place: Lemma 3.33 and its generating sets, with Rezk Section 2.5 for the cartesian structure.

proof.text: For the fixed monomorphism $f:P\to Q$ put $J_f=J_R\cup\{f\square cb_m:m\geq0\}$. If $Z$ is Reedy fibrant, the simplicial mapping axiom of [lem-coef-simplicial-space-reedy-cartesian] makes $\operatorname{Map}(f,Z)$ a Kan fibration. It is a weak equivalence exactly when it is a trivial fibration, equivalently has boundary lifting by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. The tensor--mapping adjunction identifies that boundary lifting with lifting $Z\to1$ against all $f\square cb_m$. Together with step 2, this proves $J_f^{\square}(Z\to1)$ if and only if $Z$ is $f$-local. Moreover, every $j\in J_f$ is monic, and $\operatorname{Map}(j,Z)$ is a trivial Kan fibration for every $f$-local $Z$: for an added generator, its boundary-$b_l$ lifting test is the lifting test of $\operatorname{Map}(f,Z)$ against $b_m\square b_l$, by associating the pushout products. The latter is a monomorphism (its domain is the union of the two boundary products), and a trivial Kan fibration lifts against every monomorphism, since these are precisely the Kan-model cofibrations; for $J_R$ it is step 3.

source.place: Proposition A.3.7.3 proof, local fibrancy through boundary pushout products; specialized to the original Reedy mapping sets.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-accessible-small-object-factorization] to the small set $J_f$ in the locally presentable category $\mathcal M$ and to each terminal arrow $X\to1$. This gives, functorially, $X\xrightarrow{\eta_X}RX\to1$, with $\eta_X$ in the weakly saturated closure of $J_f$ and $RX\to1$ in $J_f^{\square}$. Hence $RX$ is $f$-local by step 4. The middle-object functor in that cited statement preserves small $\kappa$-filtered colimits for some regular small $\kappa$. The functor $X\mapsto(X\to1)$ preserves such colimits: a filtered category is nonempty and connected, so the colimit of its constant terminal diagram is terminal, and arrow colimits are componentwise. Therefore $R$ preserves those colimits. This construction uses only the original Reedy structure and small-object factorization.

source.place: Proposition A.1.2.5, applied to the explicitly specified small set $J_f$.

proof.text: For an $f$-local $Z$, let $T_Z$ consist of the restriction arrows $Z^{c\Delta^m}\to Z^{c\partial\Delta^m}$ in the cartesian closed category of [lem-coef-simplicial-space-reedy-cartesian], for $m\geq0$. The tensor--mapping adjunction and the boundary criterion of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] say that $\operatorname{Map}(j,Z)$ is a trivial fibration if and only if $j\in{}^{\square}T_Z$. By step 4, $J_f\subseteq{}^{\square}T_Z$. This left lifting class contains every isomorphism $a$, since the filler of a square with top map $u$ is $ua^{-1}$. It is closed under pushouts and retracts by [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure], and under small continuous transfinite compositions by [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting]. Coproducts also preserve it, by choosing a filler independently on each summand. Thus it contains the weakly saturated closure of $J_f$. In particular $\operatorname{Map}(\eta_X,Z)$ is a trivial Kan fibration for every $X$ and every $f$-local $Z$.

source.place: Proposition A.3.7.3 proof, local equivalence of the local replacement unit; closure is proved by diagonal lifting.

proof.text: We need homotopy invariance only in the original Reedy structure. If $w:A\to B$ is a Reedy weak equivalence, factor it as a trivial cofibration $i:A\to E$ followed by a trivial fibration $p:E\to B$, using [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] and two-out-of-three. For fibrant $Z$, $\operatorname{Map}(i,Z)$ is a trivial fibration by [lem-coef-simplicial-space-reedy-cartesian]. Since all objects are cofibrant, $p$ has a section $s:B\to E$. Lift against $p$ with left map $E\times c\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow E\times c\Delta^1$, endpoint maps $sp,1_E$, and bottom map $p$ constant along the interval. This produces a simplicial homotopy $sp\simeq1_E$. If $H$ is this homotopy, the formula $(g,t)\mapsto g\circ H(-,t)$, using the same simplex parameter in $g$ and $H$, is a homotopy on $\operatorname{Map}(E,Z)$ from precomposition by $sp$ to the identity. Since $ps=1_B$, the other composite is the identity strictly. Thus $\operatorname{Map}(p,Z)$ is a simplicial homotopy equivalence with inverse $\operatorname{Map}(s,Z)$; [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak] makes it a weak homotopy equivalence. Composition proves the same for $\operatorname{Map}(w,Z)$.

source.place: Proposition A.3.7.3 proof, homotopy invariance of mapping spaces; the factorization, section, and cylinder lifting argument is supplied here.

proof.text: For any arrow $u:X\to Y$, naturality gives $Ru\,\eta_X=\eta_Yu$. Applying $\operatorname{Map}(-,Z)$ for each $f$-local $Z$, both unit maps are weak equivalences by step 6. Two-out-of-three in the Kan model structure [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] then gives: $u$ is an $f$-local equivalence if and only if $Ru$ is one. If $Ru$ is a Reedy weak equivalence, step 7 shows it is an $f$-local equivalence. Conversely suppose $v:A\to B$ is an $f$-local equivalence with $A,B$ themselves $f$-local (apply this to $Ru$). The mapping sets into either object are Kan by [lem-coef-simplicial-space-reedy-cartesian]. The weak equivalences between these Kan mapping sets induce bijections on edge components: [lem-cbc-kan-whitehead-inverse] supplies simplicial homotopy inverses. Surjectivity of $\pi_0\operatorname{Map}(v,A)$ gives $s:B\to A$ with $sv\simeq1_A$. Injectivity of $\pi_0\operatorname{Map}(v,B)$ gives $vs\simeq1_B$, since $(vs)v\simeq v$. In a Kan mapping set, an edge zigzag can be replaced by one edge by filling $2$-horns. These are simplicial homotopies using the inner cylinder. Evaluating at every outer degree gives homotopy inverses of simplicial sets; [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak] makes each $v_n$ a weak equivalence. By [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], $v$ is Reedy weakly equivalent. We have proved $u$ is $f$-locally equivalent exactly when $Ru\in W_R$.

source.place: Proposition A.3.7.3 proof, detection after local replacement; the two mapping tests give the homotopy inverse explicitly.

proof.text: Use [lem-coef-accessible-small-object-factorization] again, now for $J_R$, to factor every $v:A\to B$ functorially as $A\xrightarrow{i_v}E_v\xrightarrow{p_v}B$. The right map is a Reedy fibration by step 2. The left map is a Reedy trivial cofibration: every $J_R$ generator is one by step 3, and the class of maps left orthogonal to all Reedy fibrations is closed under pushouts, retracts and transfinite compositions by [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure] and [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting], as well as coproducts by componentwise fillers. The Reedy weak factorization system in [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] identifies this class with its trivial cofibrations. Thus two-out-of-three and step 2 show $v\in W_R$ if and only if $p_v\in I_R^{\square}$. The arrow functor $v\mapsto p_v$ preserves sufficiently filtered colimits, since its source $E_v$ does by the cited accessible small-object theorem and its target is the target of $v$. Let $T(u)=p_{Ru}$. Composing the two preserving functors gives one regular small bound (take the larger of their two bounds), so $T$ preserves sufficiently filtered colimits. Step 8 gives $T(u)\in I_R^{\square}$ exactly when $u$ is an $f$-local equivalence.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.8 proof, factorization reducing weak equivalences to trivial fibrations; applied after the replacement in steps 5--8.

proof.text: For each bidegree $(n,m)$ let $H_{n,m}=F(n)\times c\Delta^m$, the corresponding set-valued representable on $D$. Let $d_{n,m}:H_{n,m}\amalg H_{n,m}\to H_{n,m}$ be the fold. By [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection], a square with left side $d_{n,m}$ and right side $u:X\to Y$ is a pair $x,x'\in X_{n,m}$ with $u(x)=u(x')$. A filler exists exactly when $x=x'$: its restrictions to the two summands must be the prescribed elements. Consequently $u$ is bidegreewise monic exactly when it has the right lifting property against every $d_{n,m}$. This tests injectivity, including empty sets, rather than requiring existence of any preimages.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.8 proof, right-lifting encoding of conditions on arrows; fold test supplied explicitly.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal N=\mathcal M\times\mathcal M$ and let $0$ be the empty simplicial space. In $\mathcal N$ take the small set $S$ consisting of $(d_{n,m},1_0)$ for all bidegrees and $(1_0,i)$ for all $i\in I_R$. Lifting in a product category is componentwise. The extra component has left map $1_0$ and has a unique filler, so $(u,T(u))\in S^{\square}$ holds exactly when $u$ is monic and $T(u)\in I_R^{\square}$. By steps 8--10 this is precisely $u\in W_f^{\mathrm{mono}}$. The functor $G:\mathcal M^{[1]}\to\mathcal N^{[1]}$ defined by $G(u)=(u,T(u))$ preserves sufficiently filtered colimits by step 9 and componentwise colimits. Thus our desired subcategory is the full inverse image $G^{-1}(S^{\square})$, not an unproved assertion that arbitrary accessible intersections remain accessible.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.8 proof, simultaneous small lifting conditions; product encoding supplied here.

proof.text: The category $\mathcal N$ is locally presentable by step 1. Apply [lem-coef-small-right-lifting-accessibility] to its small set $S$. It says exactly that the full subcategory on $S^{\square}$ in $\mathcal N^{[1]}$ is replete and accessible as an ambient subcategory. Both $\mathcal M^{[1]}$ and $\mathcal N^{[1]}$ are locally presentable by step 1, and $G$ preserves small $\kappa$-filtered colimits for some regular small $\kappa$ by step 11. Apply [lem-coef-accessible-full-inverse-image] to $G$ and $S^{\square}$. Its conclusion for $G^{-1}(S^{\square})=W_f^{\mathrm{mono}}$ is exactly the asserted closure and small generation for some regular small $\lambda$, together with repleteness. Both small-object sets, the resulting functors, and all cardinal choices were fixed using only $f$ and the universe, not an individual arrow. No localized model structure has entered any step.

source.place: Corollaries A.2.6.7 and A.2.6.8, only inverse image and small right-lifting classes.

There are no new nodes and no unit or chapter edits. The item is not a target, so the base-change and coefficient-category check does not apply, and no SGA source is cited. The source is Barwick 4.5–4.6 (all local equivalences), with the restriction to monomorphisms honestly marked as agent-formulated; Barwick and HTT are WANTED and proof_origin is agent. The proof argues directly in the original Reedy structure. (1) Steps 2–3: the matching-object squares give J_R^□=Fib_R and I_R^□=Fib_R∩W_R, including n=0, and the pushout-product clause makes J_R trivial cofibrations. (2) Step 4: the J_f generators test f-locality; the added generators work because f□c(b_m□b_l) is monic. (3) Steps 5–6: the small-object factorization gives an accessible local replacement R, and its unit maps are trivial mapping fibrations by closure under isomorphisms, pushouts, retracts, transfinite composites and coproducts. (4) Step 7: a Reedy weak equivalence is an f-local equivalence, via a section and a cylinder lift, using the homotopy-equivalence lemma, which needs no Kan hypothesis. (5) Step 8: the converse between f-local objects uses Kan mapping sets, Whitehead, π_0 surjectivity and injectivity, and evaluation in each outer degree. (6) Steps 9–11: the J_R factorization detects W_R by I_R-lifting, fold maps detect monomorphisms (vacuous on empty sets), and the product-category set S encodes both conditions exactly, since 1_0 has a unique filler. (7) Step 12: small-right-lifting-accessibility and accessible-full-inverse-image (which allows an arbitrary arrow functor) give exactly repleteness, λ-filtered closure and small generation.
